content: Melvin-Koushki describes the second half of MS Majlis 10196 as less problematic: its works are not in chronological order, cover 829-38/1427-35, and perhaps no more than two were copied after Ibn Turka's death; he therefore assumes its dates are more likely to be, or to approximate, the date of composition, and that places named refer to the place of composition or a nearby location.
